course: I think HUM111 is fundamentally unnecessary. I thought this course would just be torture when I first got it, but turns out my interest in philosophy lead me to eventually like this course. But this does not change that it has nothing to do with my major and most of the time feels like a waste of my time. For a person who has no interest in ancient literature, philosophy and civilization theory in general; Im certain that this course will most likely be torment. Personally, I feel really lucky to have enjoyed it, otherwise I wouldn't have found any morale to study on it. I have a problem with the fact that this is a mandatory course for all students in Bilkent. The second issue comes from the fact that this course requires too much time and effort. Reading the readings are fine (although a bit annoying since you have to read the given texts every week) although the fact that you have to PRINT OUT every text and bring it to class is a struggle on its own.    There is a reading packet containing all the readings but carrying a 500 page notebook the entire semester is not an option for me due to transportation; so I had to print out every reading before class (like most of my classmates) and this got unbearable as the semester continued. In the final weeks almost no-one had a printout of the necessary texts which lead to a slight stagnation of the class. I know it's about ai or something or bla blah blah but come on, the midterm and final forms 60% of the classes grade and quizzes are 24%. The rest of the grade is participation and in-class writings. The only case for phone use to be a problem is during the in-class writings which is like 10% AND Id say it could easily be avoided with proper regulations during in-class writings. In my personal opinion, always having the ease to access the texts and notes is a good trade-off for minor ai usage by students who are uninterested in the course. They won't have access to that ai in the midterm final and quizzes regardless.

Lecturer doesn't respect people's individuality as much as he respects his own subjects. Active participation makes up 6 point of the overall grade, which is excessive considering that letter grade intervals in the humanity catalog are only 2 points each. I think it's quite selfish to expect people to constantly try to speak up among 30-40 others. Besides, students from the language department already participate quite actively in class, and those who don't are still listening. There's no need to penalize anyone with points. This is a general course provided by the university, and its purpose is to give us cultural enrichment rather than improve our participation performance. However, because of the lecturer's tactics, some of us are becoming even more disconnected from the course.

Brian Hoca süper bir insan, çok çalışkan, her ders için sunumlar hazırlıyor ve anlattığı her şey hakkında fazlasıyla bilgi sahibi. Sizi dinlerken gözünüzün içine bakıyor, bir iki söz almanızdan sonra adınızı ezberliyor ve sizi her zaman gördüğünü ve dinlediğini belli ediyor. Saçma bir şey söyleseniz bile hiç rencide olmamanız için en doğru cevabı veriyor. Puanlamasının da adil olduğunu düşünüyorum. Tek sıkıntı sizden de çok çalışmanızı bekliyor, belki başka hocaların beklediğinden daha fazla şey bekliyor bu konuda. Neredeyse her ders hem sınıf içinde yazı yazıyoruz, hem de quizlerde yazıyoruz, hem de vize ve final zaten essay formatında. Eğer fen veya mühendislik fakültesindeyseniz alışkın olmadığınız için bu kadar yazı yazmak zorlayıcı ve yorucu olabiliyor fakat bunun iyi yanı da eğer dersi iyi dinlediyseniz ve dinlediklerinizi iyi ifade ederseniz sınava çalışmadan da iyi bir puan alabilirsiniz. Tarzını diğer hocalardan farklı fakat verimli buldum. Okumalar çok güzel fakat çok fazla olması dönem içinde yorabilir.
Nazik ve anlayışlı birİ. Slaytları okuduğumuz kaynakları açıklamada yeterli.
